newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo crepe prices ease as bigger volumes seen.
newsitem.headline: Colombo crepe prices ease as bigger volumes seen.

text.p: Crepe prices eased at Thursday's Colombo rubber auction as buyers held back, anticipating increased availability following good weather.
RSS prices held firm, brokers and exporters said.
"Crepe prices fell because bigger quantities were there," said a broker at John Keells. "The market was high earlier because quantities were low."

The average price for best latex one-x was 73.50 rupees ($1.29) per kg, against 75 rupees on Tuesday, when the auction was last held. Number one was 72.50 rupees, down one rupee from Tuesday, while RSS 1 went for 65.40 on both days.
Brokers Forbes and Walker said 133 tonnes of crepe, 54 tonnes of scrap crepe and 25 tonnes of sheet were on offer.
"The market was a little easier for the top grades as people expect the rubber to come in now the weather is good," said an exporter. "There's no panic like in the rainy season."
Rain brings production to a virtual standstill and affects the quality of whatever can be tapped, brokers said.
